I'm sure you know that in civil law countries, the three countries of the three Judges on this Bench, it's up to the Judges to appoint experts. The parties must remain silent. If they are not happy with the situation, they can request a counter-expertise to challenge the conclusions drawn by the first expert. This is a possibility. But in the first place, it's up to the Judges to control the selection of the expert. So it's quite -- what you're saying is very interesting, but it should be in the Rules, and unfortunately, it is not stated in the Rules. Furthermore, thinking about Mr. Milosevic, I don't remember that at the time, the Prosecution asked for a Prosecution expert to be appointed to check on Mr. Milosevic's health. I don't think so. And I don't think that Mr. Milosevic also would have appointed his own expert, either. I believe it was the Trial Chamber which appointed the experts. I may be wrong, but I'm saying this off the cuff. But I took due note of what you said, but we have rendered our decision, and I believe that the Registrar is looking for these three experts at the moment.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: I appreciate your comments, Your Honour. And certainly to the extent that the parties or a party is allowed to participate in the assessment of experts, that, in fact, it would not just be one party participating in that process. And to the extent that it's being a list, or I'm not sure exactly what it would be, is being reviewed by a party, it should be reviewed by both parties. I say that just to make sure that we have that on the record.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Mr. Marcussen.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: I apologise. We had promised to finish. I have now received a redacted version of the financing decision that we discussed earlier, and I've looked at the redactions that have been made. And in light of those redactions, I would like to maintain the Prosecution's motion that the full decision be made public, or at least that paragraph 21 be made public in its entirety. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. We take due note of what you said, and when we rule on this --

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May I say something?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Seselj.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I fully agree that all documents pertaining to my health be placed at the disposal of the Prosecution, or, rather, that they be photocopied and submitted to the Prosecution so that they could have full insight. I have no reason to keep secret any information about the state of my health, none whatsoever. I also have no reason to exaggerate the problems that I am facing. I would not have raised that issue had it not been raised by the Trial Chamber. I forbade the Secretariat or the Registry to provide information about my health to the National Council for Co-operation with The Hague Tribunal in Belgrade. This is an organ of that regime there, and I particularly forbade them from providing information to the Military Medical Academy, because I already spoke at the last status conference about the inhumane and unprofessional behaviour of Major Mirko Jevtic, head of the Medical Military Academy. In the meantime, the Ministry of Defence intervened -- interfered, and there was this doctor who presented an opinion on my report last year of over 60 pages, and they did not let him give information to my associates. Of course, I also condemned that doctor who asked the commander to give him permission to behave ethically. But that is the problem with physicians who have officers' insignia. There will either be a doctor or an officer, and what prevails in their case is the consciousness of an officer, and that is limited. I never want to deal with doctors like that anymore. I also, in particular, do not want to have any dealings with the National Co-operation with The Hague Tribunal, especially now that they have engaged head-hunters to search for the glorious Serb general Ratko Mladic, and they promised a prize of 10 million euro. Of course, they will never find him, but what they did is immoral. What I would like the transcript to reflect is that I want the cardiovascular clinic in Moscow, Bakulyev, to be provided with my full medical documentation. It is my understanding that they're going to address the Registry during the next few days. I am saying that now, and this is recorded in the official transcript. I agree that my entire medical file be provided to them. I'm just asking for one thing in the future; that all reports about the state of my health first come into my own hands, or simultaneously in my own hands, the hands of the Trial Chamber, the prison warden, and so on. What happened before was that all others would get this before myself. Of course, I signed consent for my medical information to be provided to others, but I have not been given full information about medical matters. So the Prosecution can be made fully aware of all of this, and in this particular case, the Prosecution will not face any attempt on my part to stall these proceedings, or stop them altogether, or delay them, on account of my health. No one can conduct these proceedings without me. Don't think that under the pretext of my health conditions, someone will impose counsel on me. I will stop taking all medication, I will stop eating, and then you can try vampires, ghosts, whoever, but you're not going to try me any longer. You are not going to try me with any kind of scum sitting in this courtroom pretending to be my lawyer. If you did not manage to do that during the Prosecution case, you will succeed even less during the Defence case. Since you've extended this hearing, and since you've given the Prosecution the opportunity to say things that were completely out of order and that did not have to be discussed at all today, I needed to add this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Seselj, the Trial Chamber notes that you see no problem to have all your medical documents disclosed to the Prosecution. Tomorrow, we'll take a look and see what has not been disclosed yet. Normally, we communicate -- we disclose everything, so I can't see what hasn't been disclosed yet. But we'll look into this to make sure that the Prosecution has absolutely everything. As far as I'm concerned, you know that I'm in favour of transparency, and I don't see why we would hide anything. However, as far as Witness VS-026, I have something to add, so I would ask Mr. Registrar to please move back into closed session for a minute.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We are in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Seselj, we're back in open session. Do you have anything to add?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Mr. President. I always feel best in this courtroom, and in this courtroom I certainly -- I don't run the risk of sustaining a heart attack. But if I wait for several months for the following hearing, then there is such a danger. Why do we wait so long? And I believe that we will lose time with this witness until May. You will see. And how long is this -- will this be going on? I appeal to you to hurry up and finish this trial while I'm still alive. I suppose that it would be awkward for you, if you couldn't complete this trial, irrespective of the intentions within this Tribunal and outside and who knows which dark forces. I hope that it's in your personal interests to bring this trial to a regular end. But then, again, maybe not. How should I know? Here's what I wanted to say: I hear for the first time today that five alleged diaries of General Ratko Mladic were found two years ago, and the remainder this year, so the first thing I would like to know is whether they were found in the same house belonging to General Mladic. If, two years ago, five diaries were found and the remainder of 20-odd - who knows how many there were - where were these diaries two years ago? Is there an explanation for that? If these five volumes were found two years ago, why hasn't the OTP had this retyped for us to be able to use it more easily? And why haven't they been translated into English, if you needed it? Why wait? It seems completely illogical to me that five of Mladic's diaries were found two years ago, and the remaining this year, and it would seem in the same place. How come? Is there some sort of manipulation there? Of course, the regime is involved in this. Now, the question is: Who wrote those Mladic's diaries, and to what end, and how much time was required for an officer to be found who is capable of imitating Mladic's handwriting? There will be many questions that will be raised there. And I have two brief matters to put forward.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Please go ahead for the two brief matters.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] On the 14th of October this year, 2010, I received a confidential letter from you, an internal memorandum. Your confidential letter is dated 13 October 2009, so I received it after exactly one year, translated into Serbian. And the internal memorandum, from which we see that officials acted in line with your letter, is dated 13 November 2009. I received that on 14 October this year as well. It's a total of five pages, five pages of material which is extremely important to me, because it shows beyond any doubt that Witness 008 provided false testimony. And I received this one year later, because probably the Registry was unable to have it translated sooner. You know when I got angry when you refused to admit this set of documents that referred to the Sarajevo theatre of war, and that's when I stopped tendering any documents. I never had anything translated, either. I completely unburdened the Translation Service. But they could have translated this much earlier, since it is so important to me, and not have me receive it one year later. I could have used it several times in this trial.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Seselj, I do not remember this internal memo dated 13th of October, 2009, dating back to over a year. But according to what you say, it took over a year for the translation. I don't understand. The Legal Officer will check tomorrow with the Translation Service. What is the last point that you wanted to raise, please?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, in that letter, you raised a few questions in relation to that witness, and then the officials of the Tribunal went to the witness to put these questions to them directly. From the answers, one can see that the testimony was quite false. Perhaps I have reminded you by saying this now. I also want to say something that at first I thought I would not bring up, in the belief that this status conference would last only for an hour and a half, which is customary. However, since it's taken a bit longer, I've changed my mind, and I decided to voice my protest over the decision that you have passed to admit into evidence, without hearing this person again, the statement that this witness gave to the OTP after he had been examined in this courtroom, because the Prosecution was not happy with the effects of the questioning of that witness. I had very little time with this witness; only about half an hour. I disqualified him completely, but very swiftly, and then the Prosecution felt the need to talk to him afterwards again so that the witness could deny some of the things that were quite clear here in the courtroom. And then the Prosecution addressed you with this motion to admit into evidence this subsequent statement. May I remind you that I sent you a statement of a man that this witness had falsely referred to with relation -- with regard to certain matters. That did not go into evidence. It was verified. As for the statement that the Prosecution provided to you, we're supposed to take their word for it that that is authentic. You neglected what I had offered to you, and you admitted into evidence this statement that the Prosecution did. Theoretically, there's another thing that's possible. Eighty witnesses were heard in this courtroom. The OTP suffered a fiasco in each and every one of these cases.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]... Dr. Seselj. I'm just trying to ascertain whether or not you're talking about two different witnesses or one. The letter, I believe, addressed VS-008, but I believe he's now talking about 1033. So I'm not sure if we're talking about the same witness.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, yes, yes, you understood it properly, Ms. Biersay.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: We have not tendered any subsequent statements from VS-008, so that's the source of my confusion.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] There's no reason for you to be confused. It's this other witness that I'm talking about. We've finished dealing with the 008 a long time ago. I am presenting all of this very nicely, but perhaps you have not been following me in a focused manner. Perhaps you have a bit of a lack of oxygen too.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Seselj, I was also wondering what other witness you were mentioning. But if I understand correctly, it's Witness 1033. We all agree; right?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think that's his code, the one who came from that faraway country to testify here, if you remember. I cannot mention his name, and there is no reason for me to do so. In the beginning of the trial, we had this problem when the OTP asked for Judge Harhoff to be recused. I hope that you will now understand who I am referring to. So we had this mess with the OTP at the very beginning of these proceedings with regard to this matter, and ultimately it proved to be totally unnecessary. Now, theoretically, it is possible, because the Prosecution suffered a fiasco with regard to each and every one of these 80 witnesses, that they could talk to all of them yet again, take new statements from them in which they would deny everything that they said during cross-examination, that they will ask you to subsequently to subsequently admit this into evidence, according to this very same principle on the basis of which you admitted this one statement into evidence. That is the protest that I wanted to voice to the Trial Chamber.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. This is all in the transcript. But I, unfortunately, do not have before me the decision admitting the statement made by -- to the Prosecutor after the hearing. Whatever the case may be, the probative value of a statement under oath is always more important than a statement made without any oath. This is a rule. Therefore, when we will have our deliberations, when we weigh all the various aspects, we will look into this. So I don't remember exactly why we admitted this statement that was made after the testimony. There is probably a reason for that, but I don't have it at hand. Whatever the case may be, as I was saying, anything said under oath will be more important, unless we are talking about a false testimony. So I cannot imagine that, under oath, someone would say something, and after they would say to the Prosecutor the opposite, which would then expose them to a prosecution because of a false testimony, so this is something that would be very strange to conceive. I do not have those statements before me here. I do not remember exactly why we admitted this subsequent statement. But during the deliberation, we will give different weight as to what has been made under oath and what has been made without an oath. But I will look at what you say, because your case has been going on for several years and a lot of motions, a lot of decisions, have been issued, and we can potentially lose track. And sometimes the parties are here to refresh our memory when those memories need to be refreshed. So there we go. I believe, Mr. Seselj, that you had concluded. Apparently not. Go on.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, let me just add one thing, Mr. President. In these proceedings, indeed, there were many witnesses who undeniably perjured themselves, and no contempt proceedings were initiated. One even brought a lawyer here when the OTP established that part of the testimony provided was false, and then that lawyer was supposed to defend that witness from my possible examination going in that direction. Just remember that. And remember those two other witnesses, 008 and another one, that the OTP gave up on themselves because they realised the testimony provided had been unreliable. Then remember the witness who moved the rally of the Serb Radical Party in Mali Zvornik two years ahead and misrepresented the speeches made at that rally, and all of these speeches were published in "Velika Srbija." Remember all the things that happened here; the man who wanted to kill his wife with an axe, and the one who wanted to throw a hand-grenade on the mosque in Belgrade. All sorts of people appeared here, and then this one who ran across fields in order to participate in the execution of detainees in Ovcara, and then he was a protected witness in Belgrade, and he sent other people to prison. We've had all sorts of things here, haven't we?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I remember everything, because you know that I devote my entire life to reading all those documents. And as you said, I wish, like everybody else, for this trial to be brought to an end as soon as possible, but we need all the procedural matters to be concluded. And before the 98 bis order hearing, you know that depends on what happens with Witness VS-026, as well as the Mladic diaries, but you said this was a secondary matter. Now, I would like to know whether the Prosecution wishes to say anything more.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: No, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Thank you very much to everyone, and this trial stands adjourned.
